content:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary rollout 2026-04-11T09:12Z - 5% traffic - elevated OOMs on model-serving nodes (svc: inference-worker). Alerting oncall.

carmen: paging @liam oncall, getting noise from canary. seeing memory spikes, containers restarting.

liam: on it. looking at the canary fleet now.

rachel: noticed increased 500s in the canary for embed requests. correlates with longer sequences.

samir: any config changes in this deploy? this was a config + code release (batching + kv-cache tweak)

liam: yeah release 2026.04.11 included smaller continuous-batching changes and kv-cache TTL change to reduce cold-starts. suspect TTL change.

eva: I can pull logs. running:
```
kubectl -n inference logs -l release=canary -c worker --since=10m | grep -i oom
```

eva: lots of OOM kill lines and java heap OOM errors in one node.

carmen: can we flip the feature flag that enabled the new kv-cache behavior? feature-key: ff.kvcache.continuous_ttl

liam: attempting flag rollback via console.. if toggle fails we will rollback the canary.

ops-bot: Permission check passed for liam. Feature flag toggle requested.

liam: toggled ff.kvcache.continuous_ttl -> false :thumbsup:

rachel: still seeing one restart, but 500 rate dropped from 14% -> 6% over last 2 mins.

samir: good, but not back to baseline 0.8%. might be residual cached state or memory not freed.

carmen: recommend quick revert of the single config commit. It's a 1-line change. If toggle didn't fully mitigate, we should deploy revert to canary and then prod.

liam: I agree. prepping a revert PR.

deploy-bot: Notifying release channel and running safety checks before revert deploy.

eva: logs show the worst of the OOMs are on nodes with >200 concurrent kv keys due to TTL bump. Revert should reduce memory pressure.

samir: add a canary-only scaling bump while we revert? autoscaler seems slow.

carmen: let's avoid scaling up - it hides the bug. prefer revert + canary replay.

liam: PR created: `revert: kv-cache TTL change` -> https://git.internal/r/infra/1234

rachel: can we run the revert in canary with a shorter deploy window and auto-roll back on error? set canary 2% for 5 mins then step.

liam: deploy command:
```
deployctl rollout --service inference-worker --image gcr/redwood/inference:2026.04.10 --canary 2 --window 5m --auto-rollback
```

deploy-bot: Starting rollout. Track at https://deploys.internal/rollouts/5678

carmen: oncall handoff incoming in ~18 minutes for @liam — @rachel, @samir you are secondary contacts.

liam: watching logs and prometheus dashboards. memory usage consistently trending down on canary pods.

rachel: SLO breaches reduced, 5xx fell back to 0.9% in canary after 3 mins.

eva: running post-deploy smoke:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://canary.redwood.ai/predict -d '{"input":"test"}' | jq .
```

eva: smoke OK. responses under 120ms.

carmen: leaving short incident note for customer-impact: "minor impact to small portion of traffic during canary rollout, some customers experienced 5xx errors for ~12 minutes. No data loss." Will update after final prod rollout.

samir: once canary stable, we can promote revert to prod. plan to do staged rollouts: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 10m windows.

liam: agreed. initiating prod rollout now.

deploy-bot: Prod rollout started: https://deploys.internal/rollouts/5679

rachel: monitoring. slight latency blip during promotion but 5xx rate inside SLA.

liam: prod promotion completed to 100%.

carmen: closing the immediate incident. marking resolution: revert of KV cache TTL commit. Follow-up action: add canary memory stress test and tighten pre-merge gate for KV cache changes (owner: samir).

samir: will add a regression test and an alert threshold rule for KV memory per pod.

eva: will create a postmortem draft. tagging the oncall timeline and commands used.

carmen: tldr for ops channel: canary OOMs after KV cache TTL increase. FF toggle partially helped. Quick revert of single commit + staged rollout resolved.

liam: thanks team. will update statuspage message to customers with ETA for postmortem.

deploy-bot: Incident closed by carmen. Duration 00:42:13. Incident severity: sev2.

carmen: great job. :heart:
